San Francisco Planning, Article 10 landmark designation: Landmark No. 147, Dutch Windmill (ordinance, Planning Commission resolution and case report)
sources.label: SF Planning, landmark designation

historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 147, Dutch Windmill.

Ordered by the Park Commission on 16 April 1902 to pump water for the park, and designed by the mechanical engineer Alpheus Bull Jr., with ironwork by the Fulton Engineering and Shipbuilding Company and two Oregon pine spars given by Pope & Talbot; by 22 August 1903 John McLaren reported it built for $18,160.96, lifting 20,000 gallons an hour to the top of Strawberry Hill.

Electric pumps were installed to help the windmill; they took over the pumping entirely, the mill fell into disrepair, its spars were taken down for safety, and its machinery went for scrap in the Second World War.
